thread:
maya: Heads up — I'm seeing configmap sync flapping during staged deploys for per-model flags. Terraform PR updated the k8s configmap resource and now we're getting rollouts thrash. Anyone seen a race where multiple writers flip a checksum annotation?

liam: Can you drop the PR link? Also are we relying on checksum annotation to trigger rollout or doing `kubectl rollout restart`? If multiple things write the same annotation in parallel it will flip.

maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5832. Current flow: terraform renders the config, computes a sha1 and writes it as `metadata.annotations.config-checksum`. But sometimes two apply paths run (agent + deploy job) and checksum toggles back and forth.

chris: Hmm. Two options: 1) make ConfigMap immutable and create a new name per sha (model-config-<sha>), or 2) ensure only one writer updates the annotation (lease/mutex).

anya: Immutable CM is safer w.r.t. in-place flips but means consumers need to switch mounts. We can handle that with an init container that symlinks the current name, but it's more infra work.

liam: Another quick mitigation: switch to server-side apply with `force_conflicts=false` and ensure a single CI job does the apply. Terraform isn't great at short-lived locks though.

maya: What about using a `coordination.k8s.io` Lease created by CI (or terraform) — writer must hold lease to update annotation. That would prevent concurrent writers.

chris: Lease pattern is clean. Implementation options: small controller that acquires lease, writes CM, releases. Or a short-lived job in CI that does the same. Terraform alone can't do acquire/release semantics during apply.

anya: For an incremental approach: add a `preflight-lock` annotation that CI sets, then CI performs the update and kicks the rollout. Runtime pods should be read-only for that annotation.

deploy-bot: infra/cicd pipeline:cm-writer -> queued (waiting on lease).

liam: For hotfix: add retry+backoff to the writer so the checksum doesn't flip too fast. Also make the template deterministic (sort keys, remove timestamps) so two renderers produce identical output.

maya: Good point — I found in the rendered template we include build metadata and a non-deterministic map iteration in a template. I'll remove timestamps and force key ordering. Example snippet I'm changing: ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: model-config
  annotations:
    config-checksum: "${sha1(rendered)}"
data:
  config.json: |
    {{- /* ensure sort_keys=true in renderer */ -}}
    {{ rendered | toJson }}
```

chris: Also add an events check for debugging: `kubectl get events -n inference --field-selector involvedObject.name=model-config` — paste any repeated updates.

maya: Pasted events: ```Normal Updated 3m (x4 over 6m) configmap/model-config Updated checksum from abc123 -> def456 -> abc123``` Looks like two different renderers produced different content.

anya: That confirms nondeterminism. Remove build IDs from the payload and use `jsonencode(var)` with stable sort.

maya: Plan: 1) strip timestamps/build IDs from rendered output, 2) add deterministic key sorting in templates, 3) prototype Lease-managed writer job in CI, 4) open RFC and PR that wires the lease. I'll assign @liam and @chris for review.

liam: Ack. Ping me when PR is up, I can review the Lease job and the template changes. :thumbsup:

chris: I can look at the RFC and event logs. Also consider a short TTL on Lease so jobs don't deadlock.

maya: Thanks all — I'll open the PR in the next few hours and attach the event logs and a quick k8s job prototype.
